questions.enonce_markdown:
Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of a cross section of the spinal cord showing the components of a reflex arc.

**OR**

Describe the structure of the spinal cord. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Drawing required (no figure supplied):** draw a large, neat, roughly oval cross section of the spinal cord with the following parts, each with a label line.

- **White matter** on the outside: it contains the long myelinated nerve fibres running up and down the cord.
- **Grey matter** inside, shaped like the letter **H** or a butterfly: it contains the cell bodies of neurones and the synapses. Its two upper arms form the **dorsal horns** and the two lower arms the **ventral horns**.
- **Central canal** in the middle of the grey matter, filled with **cerebrospinal fluid**.
- **Dorsal (posterior) root**, entering at the back, with the **dorsal root ganglion** (swelling that contains the cell bodies of the sensory neurones).
- **Ventral (anterior) root**, leaving at the front and carrying motor fibres.
- The **reflex arc** drawn with arrows: **receptor** (in the skin) -> **sensory neurone** (through the dorsal root) -> **relay (intermediate) neurone** in the grey matter -> **motor neurone** (leaving through the ventral root) -> **effector** (a muscle).
- The **meninges** (protective membranes) around the cord.

**If the question is answered by description (alternative):** the spinal cord is a cylinder of nervous tissue, about 45 cm long, that runs inside the **vertebral column** from the brain stem to the lower back. It is protected by the vertebrae and by three membranes, the **meninges**, with **cerebrospinal fluid** between them. In cross section it has an outer layer of **white matter** (nerve fibres covered by a fatty myelin sheath) and an inner **H-shaped grey matter** (cell bodies and synapses) around a **central canal** filled with cerebrospinal fluid. Pairs of **spinal nerves** leave the cord: each has a **dorsal root** carrying sensory neurones (with a **ganglion**) and a **ventral root** carrying motor neurones.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the sequence of events that occurs when you mistakenly prick your finger with a needle. *(11 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is a **reflex action** (rapid, automatic and protective). The events follow the **reflex arc** in this order:

1. **Stimulus**: the sharp needle pricks the skin of the finger.
2. **Receptors**: the **pain receptors** (free nerve endings) in the skin detect the stimulus and are stimulated.
3. The receptors set up **nerve impulses** in the **sensory neurone**.
4. The impulses travel along the sensory neurone to the **spinal cord**, entering through the **dorsal root** (the cell body is in the dorsal root ganglion).
5. In the **grey matter** of the spinal cord, the sensory neurone passes the impulses across a **synapse** to a **relay (intermediate) neurone**. The synapse is crossed by a chemical transmitter (neurotransmitter) that diffuses across the gap.
6. The relay neurone passes the impulses across a second synapse to a **motor neurone**.
7. The motor neurone carries the impulses out of the spinal cord through the **ventral root** to the **effector**, the muscles of the arm (the flexor muscles, such as the biceps).
8. The **effector responds**: the muscles **contract** and the hand is **pulled away** from the needle, which prevents more damage.
9. At the same time, other impulses pass up the spinal cord to the **brain** (cerebrum), so that you become **aware of the pain** a moment after the finger has moved. The brain is therefore not needed for the movement itself, which is why the response is so fast.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is a reflex action different from learning? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Reflex action | Learning |
|---|---|
| Automatic and **involuntary**, it does not need thought | A **voluntary**, conscious process that involves the brain (cerebrum) |
| **Inborn** (inherited), the response is the same each time and is not changed by practice | **Acquired** through experience and practice; the response is improved and can be modified |
| Very fast, it follows a short pathway through the spinal cord | Slower, it needs memory and many repetitions |

(Any two differences.)
